In mathematics, a '''Pontryagin cohomology operation''' is a [[cohomology operation]] taking [[Characteristic class|cohomology classes]] in ''H''<sup>2''n''</sup>(''X'','''Z'''/''p''<sup>''r''</sup>'''Z''') to ''H''<sup>2''pn''</sup>(''X'','''Z'''/''p''<sup>''r''+1</sup>'''Z''') for some [[prime number]] ''p''. When ''p''=2 these operations were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Pontryagin|authorlink=Lev Pontryagin|year=1942}} and were named '''Pontrjagin squares''' by {{harvtxt|Whitehead|1949}} (with the term "'''Pontryagin square'''" also being used). They were generalized to arbitrary primes by {{harvtxt|Thomas|1956}}.
